**Test image features:**
- Stem at/near the soil line, partially in soil
- White cottony mycelium covering the stem
- Dark (gray-black) round sclerotia embedded in the white mycelium
- Stem appears decayed/rotted

**Key comparisons:**
- **Southern Blight** (Bugwood_23): Shows white mycelium on stem, but sclerotia are small (1-2mm), tan/mustard-brown colored — distinctly lighter than the dark sclerotia in the test image
- **Sclerotinia Timber Rot** (Bugwood_14, 23): Lab plates show white mycelium with dark gray-to-black, round, glistening sclerotia — the color and relative size match the test image much better
- **Gray Mold**: Shows brown leaf/stem lesions without sclerotia — no match
- **Alternaria Black Molds**: Shows dark stem lesions only — no match

The sclerotia in the test image are definitively **dark gray-to-black**, which is characteristic of *Sclerotinia sclerotiorum* (which produces black sclerotia when mature). *Sclerotium rolfsii* (Southern Blight) produces tan/brown, mustard-seed-sized sclerotia. The test image sclerotia are also slightly larger than typical Southern Blight sclerotia.
